conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: User primary keys differ (A: integer, B: text)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: One User entity keyed by an opaque random text id (uuid4 hex) generated by the unified app; A's integer ids and B's 'lu-<n>' ids are not reused (no persisted source data exists; a legacy_id would hold them if data were ever imported).

conflicts.subject: provider
conflicts.detail: Identity providers differ (A: own (local accounts); B: external oauth provider (google-style); C: none (authorization only))
solutions: Choose one identity provider and migrate accounts to it
Link accounts by verified email during migration
conflicts.recommended: One identity system for the unified app

resolution.decision: One identity system (the unified identity module) with two sign-in methods: local password and a federated OAuth provider behind an adapter; the provider callback data (provider, subject, email, email_verified) is the input to login_oauth. Real provider token verification is not testable here.

conflicts.subject: model
conflicts.detail: Authorization models differ (A: single role; B: single role; C: role-based access control)
solutions: Choose one authorization model and express the others' rules in it
conflicts.recommended: One authorization model with one permission check function

resolution.decision: One role-based model (C's): roles viewer/editor/admin as permission sets and one can(role, permission) check used by every privileged action.

conflicts.subject: default_role
conflicts.detail: Rule default_role differs (A: "user", B: "member")
solutions: Choose one value and record why
Make it a setting if both are legitimate
conflicts.recommended: Pick one value with the user; make it configurable only if both are needed

resolution.decision: Same as database:default-value:user.role: editor for password sign-up, viewer for a new federated account; a linked federated sign-in keeps the existing account's role.

conflicts.subject: email_case
conflicts.detail: Rule email_case differs (A: "lowercase", B: "as given")
solutions: Choose one value and record why
Make it a setting if both are legitimate
conflicts.recommended: Pick one value with the user; make it configurable only if both are needed

resolution.decision: Emails are normalised everywhere (strip, lowercase) before storage, lookup and linking; B's as-given emails are normalised.

conflicts.subject: accounts
conflicts.detail: password sign-in (A) and federated sign-in (B) will meet in one account table: the same person can arrive twice, or an attacker can claim an account through an unverified email
solutions: Link a social or SSO login to an existing account only through a verified email
Keep separate accounts and offer a manual, authenticated link step
conflicts.recommended: Never merge accounts on an unverified email: that is an account-takeover path

resolution.decision: User decision: one account per person; a federated sign-in joins an existing account only when the provider says email_verified is exactly True and the email is owned by an existing account; otherwise it is a separate account. Never link on an unverified email.

conflicts.subject: role-change-rules
conflicts.detail: C's set_role trusts a role string from the caller and accepts any new role name; the user requires that only an admin changes roles and nobody raises their own role
solutions: Resolve the caller from the session; admin only; validate the role; refuse raising one's own role
Keep C's behaviour
conflicts.recommended: Caller from session token; PermissionError unless admin; unknown role rejected; self-raise refused

resolution.decision: set_role(token, user_id, role): caller resolved from the session; PermissionError unless the caller is admin (invalid session included); role must be a known unified role (ValueError); target must exist (KeyError); nobody may raise their own role (PermissionError) (user decision).

conflicts.subject: roles
conflicts.detail: Role sets differ (A: user; B: member; C: admin, editor, viewer)
solutions: Map every source role to a unified role set and write the mapping down
Model special powers (such as approving) as permissions, not extra roles
conflicts.recommended: One role set plus explicit permissions; map every source role

resolution.decision: One role set (viewer, editor, admin) with role_mapping A:user->editor, B:member->viewer, C:viewer/editor/admin unchanged (user decision). Special powers stay permissions (manage_roles).

conflicts.subject: session
conflicts.detail: Session mechanisms differ (A: opaque bearer token in an in-memory store, no expiry; B: none in the source (callback returns the account record); C: none)
solutions: Choose one session mechanism (http-only cookie sessions are the safer default for web apps)
Use tokens only where a client cannot hold cookies
conflicts.recommended: One session mechanism for the whole app

resolution.decision: One session mechanism: an opaque random token (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)) stored only as its SHA-256, with an expiry (default 8 h, configurable), revocable by logout; both sign-in methods issue it. A web layer would carry it in an http-only secure cookie.

conflicts.subject: duplicate-registration
conflicts.detail: A overwrites an existing account when the same email registers again; with one account per person this would let anyone take over an account (including one created or linked by OAuth)
solutions: Refuse registration when the normalised email already belongs to a user
Keep A's overwrite behaviour
conflicts.recommended: Refuse a duplicate registration with AuthError; never overwrite

resolution.decision: Refuse registration when the normalised email is already owned by an account (password or verified federated); raise AuthError and never overwrite.

conflicts.subject: user.role
conflicts.detail: User.role allows different values (A only: user; B only: member; 2 values in all)
solutions: Define one value set and a mapping from every source value to it
Keep the field per source if the states really differ
conflicts.recommended: One value set with an explicit mapping; values without a mapping block the migration

resolution.decision: One value set: viewer, editor, admin. Mapping A user->editor, B member->viewer, C roles unchanged (user decision in task.md); unknown source roles raise KeyError.

conflicts.subject: user.email
conflicts.detail: User.email (A:email, B:email) means different things (A: 'lowercased; the dict key'; B: 'as sent by the provider, not normalised, not unique')
solutions: Keep two fields with distinct names (for example owner_id and created_by)
Merge them only if the user confirms they mean the same
conflicts.recommended: Ask the user; never merge fields because their names match or an alias says so

resolution.decision: User.email is the person's normalised (trimmed, lowercased) email. A's lowercased key and B's provider email are kept apart from ownership: a PasswordCredential owns its email (unique), a federated Identity records the provider's email and whether it was verified; only owned emails are used for linking.

conflicts.subject: user.id
conflicts.detail: User.id (A:id, B:id) means different things (A: 'len(USERS)+1 at registration'; B: ''lu-' plus a counter')
solutions: Keep two fields with distinct names (for example owner_id and created_by)
Merge them only if the user confirms they mean the same
conflicts.recommended: Ask the user; never merge fields because their names match or an alias says so

resolution.decision: Neither source id survives: A's counter and B's 'lu-' counter are both replaced by one generated opaque id; the meaning is 'the unified user's id'.

conflicts.subject: user.id
conflicts.detail: User.id types differ (A: integer, B: text)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: User.id is text (uuid4 hex) for every user; see database:primary-key:user.

conflicts.subject: methods
conflicts.detail: Sign-in methods differ (A: password; B: oauth)
solutions: Offer the union of kept sign-in methods through one identity system
Drop sign-in methods no kept feature needs
conflicts.recommended: One identity system that offers the sign-in methods kept features need

resolution.decision: Offer both kept methods, password and OAuth, through the one identity system.

conflicts.subject: first-admin
conflicts.detail: Only an admin can grant admin, and no source creates the first admin
solutions: A setup-only bootstrap_admin that works only while no admin exists
Seed an admin from configuration
conflicts.recommended: bootstrap_admin(email, password) for setup; refused once an admin exists

resolution.decision: bootstrap_admin(email, password) creates the first admin for setup only and is refused (PermissionError) once any admin exists.

conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: deleting a User means different things (A: hard, B: hard delete (no marker found))
solutions: Choose soft or hard delete for the merged entity and convert the other source's rows
Keep deleted rows from the soft-delete source as archived
conflicts.recommended: Soft delete for merged data unless the user decides otherwise

resolution.decision: No delete feature is kept in either source slice and none is built; deletion is out of scope (recorded in the PRD). If added later: hard delete plus session revocation.

conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: User exists in A:User, B:Account; fields not shared: hash (only A), provider (only B), salt (only A), subject (only B)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge only once it is confirmed they mean the same thing; then list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge A:User and B:Account into one User (alias recorded with reason); sign-in methods become child records: PasswordCredential (A's email, salt, hash) and Identity (B's provider, subject, email, email_verified).

conflicts.subject: user.email
conflicts.detail: User.email is A: required, B: optional
solutions: Keep the field nullable
Make it required with a default for rows that have no value
conflicts.recommended: Do not make a field required until every source row has a value or a default is agreed

resolution.decision: User.email optional (a provider may send none); password users always have one; a federated sign-in without an email never links.

conflicts.subject: user.role
conflicts.detail: User.role defaults differ (A: "user", B: "member")
solutions: Choose one default and record why
conflicts.recommended: One default, chosen with the user

resolution.decision: Default role depends on how the account was created: password registration gets map_source_role('A','user') = editor; a new federated account gets map_source_role('B','member') = viewer (user decision).
